newsitem.title: INDIA: India call at 0.5-1.0 pct, easy despite auctions.
newsitem.headline: India call at 0.5-1.0 pct, easy despite auctions.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in 0.5-1.0 percent range in early Tuesday trade, marginally up from Monday's close of 0.1-0.4 percent, dealers said.
They said funds outflows towards auctions held by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday had not affected liquidity much and call money was expected to remain easy.

The RBI conducted two auctions on Monday - a 10-year bond auction for 30 billion rupees and a four-day repo auction of government securities. It accepted bids for a total of 81.30 billion rupees at the two auctions.
"The net outflow is mainly the 30 billion towards the 10-year bonds," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
He said subscriptions towards the repo were offset by the reversal of an earlier repo auction held on April 15.

"Repurchase of 42.67 billion rupees for the April 15 auction takes place today," the dealer said. "The main factor to consider from the liquidity angle is the number of bids rejected by RBI at yesterday's auctions."
The central bank rejected bids for 51.50 billion rupees at the repo auction and rejected bids for 51.14 billion at the 10-year bond auction.
"This means there is more than 100 billion rupees of surplus funds with the banking system," the dealer said. "Call rates will remain easy."
